chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Hafs ibn Salim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Taslim (salutation) in the two Rak'at of Al-Witr, so he said: 'Yes, and if you have a need, go out and fulfill it, then return and bow in one Rak'ah.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْوَتْرِ: The two Rak'at of Witr prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Taslim in the two Rak'at of Witr prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the Witr prayer structure, permitting the worshipper to conclude the two Rak'at with Taslim if they have an urgent need, thereby allowing for a break before completing the final unit. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*rukhas*) in optional prayers, distinguishing the Witr from obligatory prayers where the final Taslim marks the definitive end. The instruction to return and perform a single Ruku' suggests a method of completing the prayer without necessarily performing a full new Rak'ah, emphasizing the spiritual utility of the prayer over rigid formalism.
